answer: In a ferrous scrap market, job allocation uses a lottery weighted by verified throughput rather than account count. A signed weighbridge receipt creates one nontransferable capacity credit per ton, and entering a draw spends that credit. Ten aliases at one depot still share the same credits, so a fable about a ripple of phantom tonnage cannot multiply their odds; an attacker must buy real scrap or bribe a weighbridge operator. Random physical audits and penalties on the operator limit forged receipts, though honest small depots may be underrepresented and need a base allocation.
